Features still being tried, off until turned on
These change how the app works in ways that may not suit every source or device. Each one is off until you turn it on, and turning it off again puts things back as they were.

An online chapter fetches up to three pages at a time instead of one, so the pages ahead are ready sooner. A source that limits how often it may be asked can answer more slowly or refuse a page, which then shows its retry button. It applies to chapters opened after the change.

Shows one title from several sources as one library entry with one chapter list, so a chapter one source lacks comes from another. Merge entries from an entry\'s menu, a library selection or the duplicate question. Each source stays a whole entry of its own, and merges sync between devices. Turning this off shows the entries separately again.
Open shared text and search requests

Adds Saikou to the share menu, so sharing a title or a web page searches your sources for it, and lets other apps, such as an extension\'s link handler, open a search here. A page from a site one of your sources reads opens that source\'s own search. Each search another app sends asks your sources, as one you type does. Off, other apps cannot send Saikou a search.

Lets you set how many days apart an entry is checked, from its Update interval dialog, instead of the estimate from its release dates. The library\'s Custom update interval filter finds those entries. The setting stays on this device and is not in backups. Turning this off puts every entry back on its estimate.

Adds a play button to the reader\'s menu in long strip that scrolls the pages by itself at the speed you set in the reader settings. Any touch stops it, and the screen stays on while it runs. The setting stays on this device and is not in backups.

Once a day on Wi-Fi, Saikou checks your extension stores and installs the updates it finds. An update signed with a different key still waits for you. A new version can change how a source behaves or break it.
Download from several sources at once

Downloads one chapter from each of several sources at the same time, instead of one chapter at a time. Chapters from the same source still download one after another, in queue order. While it is on, Settings > Downloads shows Sources downloaded at once, which sets how many. Uses more data, memory and battery while downloads run. A change applies from the next chapter to start.

Lets the left to right and right to left paged modes show two pages at once, as a printed book does: in landscape, always or never, as you choose in the reader settings. The first page and wide pages stand alone, wide pages whole rather than split or rotated, and Shift pages in the reader\'s menu moves the pairing by one page for that entry. Experimental: until a page has loaded its size is a guess, so a pair can change as wide pages turn up. The setting stays on this device and is not in backups.

Lets sources load through an ad blocker, a DNS filter or a network that inspects secure connections with a certificate you installed on this device. Whoever controls that certificate can read and change what Saikou loads from sources. Sync, tracking, extension stores and app updates keep trusting only the certificates Android ships with. Takes effect after a restart.

New downloads are saved as one .cbz file per chapter instead of a folder of images, which other readers and file managers open more easily. Each chapter takes a moment longer to finish while its pages are packed into the file. Chapters you already downloaded stay as they are.
